reviewer: IBM Bob (Bob Shell `bob run`, ask mode)
summary: The commit was authored by a human (record.json: "kind": "human", "mode": "origit-build") and made no agent reads (record.json: "read": []). It installs the entire Origit agentic-review infrastructure into the repository's agent-configuration directory: a new origit-review mode with execute permissions, a new MCP server wired to a developer's local venv path, three refactored lifecycle hook scripts, a new skill file, and two new rules files that will govern all future AI reviewer sessions. Because every changed file lives under .bob/ — the directory that defines the agent's identity, permissions, tools, and behaviour — the dominant exposure surface is persistent context poisoning (ASI06) and supply-chain registration (ASI04); ASI01 is flagged at medium by the pre-filter for the same files but no hidden-text payload was found.

categories.title: Agent Goal Hijack
categories.evidence: prefilter.json lines 5-84: nine separate ASI01 findings, each with reason "agent config changed", covering .bob/custom_modes.yaml, .bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh, .bob/hooks/origit-session-commit.sh, .bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh, .bob/mcp.json, .bob/rules-origit-review/01-owasp-agentic-top10.md, .bob/rules-origit-review/02-evidence-rules.md, .bob/settings.json, .bob/skills/origit/SKILL.md. prefilter.json line 86: "hidden_text": []. record.json line 13: "read": [].
categories.rationale: The deterministic pre-filter identified nine agent-configuration files modified in this commit as ASI01 candidates. No hidden Unicode-tag or zero-width text was detected (hidden_text is empty), and the record shows the agent read nothing, so there is no evidence of an instruction-injection payload. The finding is retained at the pre-filter's medium severity because the changed files define the agent's goals and rules for future sessions.

categories.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 36-39 (.bob/custom_modes.yaml, origit-review mode): "groups: - read - - execute - description: Read-only commands (origit show/log/taint, git show/log) - todo". diff.patch lines 173, 197, 210, 227 (.bob/settings.json): hooks calling "sh .bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh session start", "sh .bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh run start", "sh .bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh trace", "sh .bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh run end" on every lifecycle event. diff.patch lines 53-54 (.bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh): iterates a list of candidate binaries and execs whichever is found first: "if [ -n \"$c\" ] && [ -x \"$c\" ]; then \"$c\" \"$@\" --root . 2>>.origit/hook-errors.log; exit 0; fi".
categories.rationale: The commit wires shell execution into every Bob lifecycle event (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop) and grants the new origit-review mode an execute permission group, broadening the shell-invocation surface for any future agent running in this repository. The hook dispatcher resolves the binary to run from environment variables and git config before falling back to PATH, which means any agent or user who can influence ORIGIT_BIN, the git config key origit.bin, or PATH can redirect what is executed on every prompt submission.

categories.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
categories.evidence: record.json line 13: "read": []. diff.patch: no .env, credential, key, token, or secret file is added or referenced in any changed file.
categories.rationale: No credentials, secrets, or sensitive identity material appear anywhere in the diff, and the agent read no files that could have exposed them.

categories.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 99-116 (.bob/mcp.json, new file): registers a new MCP server: "\"origit\": { \"command\": \"/home/timotej/Documents/bcco/code/origit/origit/.venv/bin/origit\", \"args\": [\"mcp\"], \"alwaysAllow\": [\"origit_taint\",\"origit_show\",\"origit_log\"] }". diff.patch lines 238-249 (.bob/skills/origit/SKILL.md, new file): registers a new skill referencing the same MCP tools. diff.patch lines 117-155 (.bob/rules-origit-review/01-owasp-agentic-top10.md and 02-evidence-rules.md, new files): two new rules files loaded into the agent's context for every review session.
categories.rationale: A new MCP server binary, a new skill, and two new rules files are introduced simultaneously. The MCP server is referenced by an absolute local filesystem path inside a developer's home directory, making it non-reproducible across environments and unverifiable by other reviewers. alwaysAllow bypasses the normal tool-approval gate for three tools. No version pin, checksum, or integrity assertion accompanies any of these new supply-chain components.

categories.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 53-54 (.bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh): "for c in \"$ORIGIT_BIN\" \"$(git config --get origit.bin 2>/dev/null)\" \"$(command -v origit 2>/dev/null)\" ...; do if [ -n \"$c\" ] && [ -x \"$c\" ]; then \"$c\" \"$@\" --root . 2>>.origit/hook-errors.log; exit 0; fi; done". diff.patch lines 173, 197, 210, 227 (.bob/settings.json): the hook is called on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, and Stop with user-controlled arguments passed through "$@". record.json line 11: "commands": [].
categories.rationale: The hook dispatcher constructs the executable path from the environment variable ORIGIT_BIN and from git config, both of which are attacker-influenced surfaces. The positional arguments passed as "$@" originate from the hook invocation strings in settings.json; however, the binary that runs is resolved at execution time from untrusted sources, creating a code-execution path where a manipulated ORIGIT_BIN or git config entry points to a malicious binary that is invoked automatically on every user prompt submission.

categories.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
categories.evidence: diff.patch line 1: "diff --git a/.bob/custom_modes.yaml". diff.patch line 40: "diff --git a/.bob/hooks/origit-hook.sh" (new file). diff.patch line 60: "diff --git a/.bob/hooks/origit-session-commit.sh". diff.patch line 75: "diff --git a/.bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh". diff.patch line 94: "diff --git a/.bob/mcp.json" (new file). diff.patch line 117: "diff --git a/.bob/rules-origit-review/01-owasp-agentic-top10.md" (new file). diff.patch line 143: "diff --git a/.bob/rules-origit-review/02-evidence-rules.md" (new file). diff.patch line 156: "diff --git a/.bob/settings.json". diff.patch line 233: "diff --git a/.bob/skills/origit/SKILL.md" (new file).
categories.rationale: Nine files inside .bob/ — the directory that controls the agent's mode definitions, lifecycle hooks, MCP tool registrations, rules, and skills — are modified or newly created in a single commit. This is a direct, high-severity ASI06 finding: any future AI agent session in this repository will operate under the new modes, hooks, rules, and tools installed here, meaning this commit persistently alters the context and behaviour of all subsequent agent sessions.

categories.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 99-116 (.bob/mcp.json): MCP server registered with "alwaysAllow": ["origit_taint","origit_show","origit_log"]. diff.patch lines 100-103: transport is a local process ("command": "/home/timotej/…/origit", "args": ["mcp"]) with no authentication or integrity fields declared.
categories.rationale: The MCP server is registered with alwaysAllow for three tools, bypassing human-in-the-loop approval for those tool calls. The local stdio transport carries no authentication token or message-signing configuration, so any process that can write to the MCP server's stdin can inject tool responses without integrity verification.

categories.title: Cascading Failures
categories.evidence: record.json: no "propagated" field present. prefilter.json: no ASI08 finding.
categories.rationale: No Origit propagation chain is recorded for this commit; cascading-failure analysis requires a prior tainted commit that this commit consumed.

categories.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 20-39 (.bob/custom_modes.yaml, origit-review mode roleDefinition): "You are the Origit security reviewer, a read-only subagent … You never edit files and never run git commands that change state." Yet the same mode's groups field (line 36-39) grants execute permissions: "- - execute - description: Read-only commands (origit show/log/taint, git show/log)". diff.patch line 29 (customInstructions): "Steps: run \`origit show <sha> --json\` … and \`git show <sha>\` with execute_command".
categories.rationale: The roleDefinition presented to human approvers describes the mode as strictly read-only, but the permission groups actually grant execute access and the customInstructions direct the agent to run shell commands. An approver reading only the roleDefinition would receive a misleading impression of the mode's actual capability surface.

categories.title: Rogue Agents
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 156-232 (.bob/settings.json): PreToolUse hook removed (lines 186-198 deleted); Stop timeout increased from 90 to 120 seconds (line 227 vs deleted line 222). diff.patch lines 60-74 (.bob/hooks/origit-session-commit.sh): original inline session-commit logic (7 lines) replaced with a one-line exec shim: "exec sh \"$(dirname \"$0\")/origit-hook.sh\" run end". diff.patch lines 75-93 (.bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh): original inline trace logic (11 lines) replaced with a one-line exec shim: "exec sh \"$(dirname \"$0\")/origit-hook.sh\" trace".
categories.rationale: The removal of the PreToolUse hook eliminates a tracing checkpoint that fired before every tool invocation, reducing the observable surface for detecting out-of-scope tool use. Consolidating both the trace and session-commit hooks into a single dispatcher (origit-hook.sh) means a compromise or misconfiguration of that one file silently disables all lifecycle instrumentation, which could allow a rogue agent to act outside its mandate without leaving a trace.
